classification.difficultyReason: Apply circumference to a capacity problem and round down to satisfy the minimum spacing.

content.prompt:
Darling Harbour is planning to install a new Ferris wheel. The wheel has a diameter of 80 m.
The pods can carry 10 passengers each but need to be spaced out by at least 10 m around the circumference of the Ferris wheel.
What is the maximum number of passengers that can be on the Ferris wheel at one time?

answer.short: 250 passengers (25 pods; round down to satisfy the minimum spacing).
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}C &= \pi\times80=80\pi\text{ m}\\\text{Number of pods} &\leq \frac{80\pi}{10}=8\pi\\8\pi &\approx 25.13\end{align*}$$
The maximum whole number of pods is 25, since the spacing must be at least 10 m.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Maximum passengers} &= 25\times10\\\text{Maximum passengers} &= 250\end{align*}$$
